newsitem.title: USA: Medicare patients said happy with managed care.
newsitem.headline: Medicare patients said happy with managed care.

text.p: Most Medicare recipients using managed care were satisfied with their coverage but were more likely than those in traditional insurance plans to complain of problems with access to care, a study said Wednesday.

The survey of 3,080 Medicare recipients for the Physician Payment Review Commission, a government-funded congressional advisory board, was the most in-depth look to date at how they were faring under health maintenance organizations.

It found only about 13 percent of Medicare enrollees reported having one or more specific access problems under managed care, and 90 percent would recommend their health maintenance organization to someone else.

However, individuals in managed care were three times as likely to report problems with access to care as those in fee-for-service plans, although the PPRC said it was difficult to make direct comparisons between the two.

"Access is generally very good for most beneficiaries, but some vulnerable groups, such as the non-elderly disabled and those in fair or poor health have more problems," said Gail Wilensky, chairman of the PPRC, said in testimony prepared for a Senate subcommittee hearing Wednesday.
The report came as Congress and the White House prepared to reopen the debate over reforming Medicare, which provides health coverage for senior citizens.

As of Nov. 1 more than 4.7 million beneficiaries were enrolled in 333 Medicare managed care plans. Unsuccessful reform plans put forward by Republicans last year provided new incentives for senior citizens to enter managed care.

Reflecting White House policy, the federal Health Care Financing Administration said in testimony, "Medicare beneficiaries themselves must determine the pace of the program's movement to managed care. The emphasis must be on choice."
